(frog-xyz)=
# frog-xyz

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-primary}`Parsing` Write the final geometry of ORCA/Gaussian calculations to XYZ files.

## What it does

After an optimisation you usually need the final structure as a plain XYZ file: to open it in a
viewer, to start the next calculation (frequencies, TD-DFT, a better single point), or to put it
in a conformer workflow. ORCA writes `<job>.xyz` itself but Gaussian does not, and when you have
many outputs (or only the output left on your laptop) extracting the last geometry by hand is
tedious. This command does it for any number of files at once.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-xyz/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

ORCA (`.out`) or Gaussian (`.log`/`.out`) **output files**, also gzipped (`.out.gz`); any job type
that prints coordinates. The **last** geometry in the file is taken, i.e. the optimised one if the
optimisation finished, or the last step reached if it did not (check the output for
convergence first: this command does not). An `.xyz` file is also accepted (its first frame is
re-written).

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | ORCA/Gaussian output files (the last geometry of each is written) |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| File | `<stem>_final.xyz` | always | Final geometry of each input (Å) |

### How to read it

One `<stem>_final.xyz` per input (standard XYZ: number of atoms, a comment line
`FROG formatted`, then element and x y z in Å). Charge and multiplicity are **not** stored
in an XYZ file: remember them for the next input.

* Files without a readable geometry are skipped with a warning and the command ends with an error
  listing them; the other files are still written.
* The input file is never overwritten; an existing `<stem>_final.xyz` is.

Example: `frog-xyz opt.out water.xyz --out-dir xyzout` writes `xyzout/opt_final.xyz` (96 atoms)
and `xyzout/water_final.xyz`.

## Step by step

1. Run `frog-xyz opt.out`: writes `opt_final.xyz` next to `opt.out`.
2. For many files use a wildcard and collect the results in one folder: `frog-xyz conf_*.out --out-dir geoms`.
3. Open the XYZ in a viewer, or paste it into the next input (ORCA: `* xyzfile 0 1 opt_final.xyz`).

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-xyz --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-xyz --help`
```text
usage: frog-xyz [-h] [-v] [-q] [--out-dir DIR] file [file ...]

Write the final geometry of ORCA/Gaussian calculations to XYZ files.

One XYZ file is written per input, next to it (or in --out-dir). The input is never overwritten.

positional arguments:
  file           ORCA/Gaussian output files (the last geometry of each is written)

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit

output:
  -v, --verbose  Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet    Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --out-dir DIR  Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file)

outputs:
  files (next to each input, or --out-dir):
    <stem>_final.xyz            Final geometry of each input (Å)

examples:
  frog-xyz opt.out
      Write opt_final.xyz next to opt.out
  frog-xyz conf_*.out --out-dir geoms
      Write one XYZ per conformer into geoms/

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-xyz.md.
```
:::
